title: Toolpath direction arrows hide the path: draw fewer, solid arrows in a second colour

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Reported by the maintainer in chat, 2026-11-16:

> "the small green movements lines ina generated path has arrow direction that is really confusing the UI making it hard to distinghuis path from direction indication.. Make the arrow a small "solid painted" arrow in teal color or something. paint about 1/3 of arrows instead or even fewer maybe.."

What happens: the viewport draws a direction arrow on the green moves of a generated toolpath. The arrows have the same colour and line style as the path, and there are many of them. The user cannot tell the path from the direction marks.

Wanted:

- The arrow is a small solid (filled) arrow head, not line strokes.
- The arrow has a colour that is different from the path colour. The maintainer proposes teal. The colour comes from the theme and is readable in each shipped theme.
- The viewport draws about one third of the arrows of today, or fewer. Space the arrows by distance on the screen or along the path, so that short moves do not collect arrows.
- The arrow size stays small at each zoom level.

Rules:

- This is a display change only. It changes no toolpath, no verify result and no posted G-code.
- The arrow geometry is precalculated and cached with the toolpath draw data. An unchanged frame does no work in proportion to the move count (frame cost rule, #2238).

Done means: a structural or scene test pins the arrow count for a recorded toolpath (one third of the old count or less) and that the arrows are filled triangles with the theme's arrow colour; the PR has before and after screenshots.
